info.title: ScoutBoy API
info.description: ScoutBoy - real-life football player discovery. Discovery spans every player-season in the connected local snapshots; configured RoleFit analysis covers attacking and midfield roles only. Every score/badge/value is explainable.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: Case-insensitive literal substring across player name, club, league and primary position. When the WHOLE input is a configured club alias ('psg', 'spurs') the clubs it names are searched as well, so club abbreviations work here too.
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal substring across player name, club, league and primary position. When the WHOLE input is a configured club alias ('psg', 'spurs') the clubs it names are searched as well, so club abbreviations work here too.

parameters.name: position_group

schema.description: 'ATT', 'MID', 'DEF' or 'GK'. Validated against the domain's discoverable position groups; an unknown value is a 422.
schema.title: Position Group

parameters.description: 'ATT', 'MID', 'DEF' or 'GK'. Validated against the domain's discoverable position groups; an unknown value is a 422.

parameters.name: role

schema.description: A configured role key. Only players with a STORED rating for it qualify, and the result's role context becomes that role: its stored score and confidence do the filtering, the ordering, the confidence tie-break and the display. An unknown role key is a 422.
schema.title: Role

parameters.description: A configured role key. Only players with a STORED rating for it qualify, and the result's role context becomes that role: its stored score and confidence do the filtering, the ordering, the confidence tie-break and the display. An unknown role key is a 422.

parameters.name: league

schema.description: Case-insensitive literal substring over the competition's slug, name and country, so 'Premier League', 'eng' and 'England' all match. A small deterministic misspelling table is applied first (see configs/discovery/search_aliases_v1.yaml); there is no fuzzy matching.
schema.title: League

parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal substring over the competition's slug, name and country, so 'Premier League', 'eng' and 'England' all match. A small deterministic misspelling table is applied first (see configs/discovery/search_aliases_v1.yaml); there is no fuzzy matching.

parameters.name: club

schema.description: Case-insensitive literal substring over the team's slug and canonical name. A deterministic alias table resolves common abbreviations and nicknames first - 'psg', 'P.S.G.', 'spurs', 'thfc' - and an ambiguous abbreviation returns every club it defensibly names. Anything that is not a configured alias is searched as an ordinary substring; there is no fuzzy matching.
schema.title: Club

parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal substring over the team's slug and canonical name. A deterministic alias table resolves common abbreviations and nicknames first - 'psg', 'P.S.G.', 'spurs', 'thfc' - and an ambiguous abbreviation returns every club it defensibly names. Anything that is not a configured alias is searched as an ordinary substring; there is no fuzzy matching.

parameters.name: nationality

schema.description: Case-insensitive literal SUBSTRING of the stored nationality, so 'Eng' matches England. A player with no stored nationality fails an active predicate rather than matching.
schema.title: Nationality

parameters.description: Case-insensitive literal SUBSTRING of the stored nationality, so 'Eng' matches England. A player with no stored nationality fails an active predicate rather than matching.

parameters.name: min_minutes

schema.description: Whole season minutes, 0-10000 inclusive. Omit for no minutes threshold; 0 is a real accepted value, not 'unset'. Unrelated to the RoleFit scale.
schema.title: Min Minutes

parameters.description: Whole season minutes, 0-10000 inclusive. Omit for no minutes threshold; 0 is a real accepted value, not 'unset'. Unrelated to the RoleFit scale.

schema.description: Applicable-role-context RoleFit floor on the authoritative 0-99 scale.
schema.title: Rolefit Min

parameters.description: Applicable-role-context RoleFit floor on the authoritative 0-99 scale.

parameters.name: rolefit_max

schema.description: Applicable-role-context RoleFit ceiling on the authoritative 0-99 scale.
schema.title: Rolefit Max

parameters.description: Applicable-role-context RoleFit ceiling on the authoritative 0-99 scale.

parameters.name: value_min

schema.description: Absolute EUR. Requires a KNOWN expected-asking high endpoint, which must reach this floor; a player with unknown market information fails rather than being read as 0.
schema.title: Value Min

parameters.description: Absolute EUR. Requires a KNOWN expected-asking high endpoint, which must reach this floor; a player with unknown market information fails rather than being read as 0.

parameters.name: value_max

schema.description: Absolute EUR. Requires a KNOWN expected-asking low endpoint at or below this ceiling. Rejected when value_min exceeds value_max.
schema.title: Value Max

parameters.description: Absolute EUR. Requires a KNOWN expected-asking low endpoint at or below this ceiling. Rejected when value_min exceeds value_max.

parameters.name: sort

schema.description: One of: rolefit_desc, rolefit_asc, age_asc, age_desc, value_desc, value_asc, name_asc. Unknown values are a 422 rather than a silent fallback. RoleFit modes order by the applicable role context's stored score and break ties on its stored confidence; the asking-price modes order by expected_asking_low_eur with unknown lower bounds last in both directions. 'age_desc' is API-only: the Discovery Sort control does not offer it.
schema.title: Sort

parameters.description: One of: rolefit_desc, rolefit_asc, age_asc, age_desc, value_desc, value_asc, name_asc. Unknown values are a 422 rather than a silent fallback. RoleFit modes order by the applicable role context's stored score and break ties on its stored confidence; the asking-price modes order by expected_asking_low_eur with unknown lower bounds last in both directions. 'age_desc' is API-only: the Discovery Sort control does not offer it.

parameters.name: scope

schema.description: 'analyzed' (default), 'all_records', or 'high_coverage_u23'. Still a supported API capability; the Discovery UI no longer exposes a selector for it and always requests the default.

schema.description: Legacy age filter: 'all' (default), 'u23', '24_26', '27_30', or '31_plus'. Superseded by the one-sided age_min / age_max bounds the Discovery age control writes; retained so existing callers keep working.

schema.description: Legacy alias: 'mvp' maps to high_coverage_u23; 'all' maps to all_records. Ignored when scope is supplied.

schema.title: Response Rating Runs Api Admin Rating Runs Get

get.description:
The signed-in account's canonical ordered My Favorites list.

Performs no write. An account that has never saved anything has no row, and
the honest answer for it is the empty list - not a freshly inserted row.

401.description: Missing, malformed, expired, forged or misscoped token.

503.description: This deployment has no identity provider configured.

put.description:
Idempotently add a player.

The player is checked before the insert, so a stale browser id becomes an
honest 404 rather than a dangling reference that would resolve to nothing on
the next read.

401.description: Missing, malformed, expired, forged or misscoped token.

503.description: This deployment has no identity provider configured.

delete.description:
Idempotently remove a player.

Deliberately does NOT 404 on an unknown player: the caller's goal is "this
player is not on my list", and that is already true. Removing something a
previous request removed is a success, so a retried delete behaves the same
as the first attempt.

Also deliberately does not CREATE an account row. A removal stores nothing,
so an account with no row already satisfies the request; inserting one would
be a write with no purpose whose only effect is to falsify "browsing writes
nothing".

401.description: Missing, malformed, expired, forged or misscoped token.

503.description: This deployment has no identity provider configured.

post.description:
Union a guest's browser-local list into the signed-in account.

Existing account favourites keep their order; previously unseen guest IDs are
appended in guest order. Duplicates collapse to their first occurrence and
unresolvable IDs are reported rather than saved, so the client can retire its
guest list on the strength of this response alone.

401.description: Missing, malformed, expired, forged or misscoped token.

503.description: This deployment has no identity provider configured.

409.description: A concurrent change prevented the merge from completing; retry.

CalibrationMeta.title: CalibrationMeta
CalibrationMeta.description:
Compact, evidence-honest calibration status for the Methodology surface.

When calibration cannot be evaluated in this environment, ``available`` is False and
``status`` is ``inconclusive`` — totals stay zero and ``config_hash`` is null rather than
fabricating a successful result or hiding the section.

DiscoverySearchResponse.title: DiscoverySearchResponse
DiscoverySearchResponse.description:
One page of Discovery results, plus which ordering produced them.

The five pagination fields are exactly the ones ``Paginated`` has always
carried, in the same shape, so every existing client keeps working unchanged.
``ranking`` is additive.

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Player IDs in canonical order: oldest saved first, with the stable row id breaking ties inside a single merge.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of players on the account's list.

changed.title: Changed
changed.description: True when this request altered the list, false when it was already in that state.

FavoriteMutationResponse.title: FavoriteMutationResponse
FavoriteMutationResponse.description:
The canonical list after a single add or remove, plus what changed.

`changed` is false when the request was a no-op — favouriting a player that
was already saved, or removing one that was not. Both are successes: the
endpoints are idempotent, so the caller can retry a dropped request without
reasoning about whether the first attempt landed.

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Ordered guest favourite player IDs. Duplicates are collapsed to their first occurrence; IDs that do not resolve to a player are reported back rather than saved.

FavoritesMergeRequest.title: FavoritesMergeRequest
FavoritesMergeRequest.description: A guest's browser-local list, offered to the account it just signed in to.

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Player IDs in canonical order: oldest saved first, with the stable row id breaking ties inside a single merge.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of players on the account's list.

added.title: Added
added.description: Guest IDs that were not on the account and have now been appended, in guest order.

already_present.title: Already Present
already_present.description: Guest IDs the account had already saved. Their existing position is unchanged.

unknown.title: Unknown
unknown.description: Guest IDs that resolve to no player. Nothing was saved for these.

FavoritesMergeResponse.title: FavoritesMergeResponse
FavoritesMergeResponse.description:
The canonical list after a merge, and an honest account of each input ID.

The three disposition lists are disjoint and together cover every distinct ID
the request offered, so a client can tell exactly what happened to a guest
list rather than inferring it from a length change.

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Player IDs in canonical order: oldest saved first, with the stable row id breaking ties inside a single merge.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of players on the account's list.

FavoritesResponse.title: FavoritesResponse
FavoritesResponse.description:
The authenticated account's canonical, ordered favourite player IDs.

Every field is REQUIRED. A Pydantic `default_factory` would publish these as
optional in the OpenAPI contract, which would be a lie about a response the
server always sends in full - and would force every consumer to write a
`?? []` that can never actually fire.

PlayerSearchCard.title: PlayerSearchCard
PlayerSearchCard.description:
One Discovery result.

Two role contexts are reported side by side and never conflated:

* ``best_role*`` is the player's own highest stored role rating, independent of
  the query. It always describes the best role, whatever was filtered.
* ``result_role*`` is the stored rating this result was actually filtered and
  ordered by, and is what a row displays. With no ``role`` filter it is the
  best-role rating; with ``role=<key>`` it is that role's stored rating.

``result_role_source`` says which of the two the caller is looking at. Nothing
here is recomputed: every score and confidence is the stored value.

RankingExplanation.title: RankingExplanation
RankingExplanation.description:
Which ordering this page is in.

Ordering only. It does not describe recruitment quality, suitability or
priority, and no filter appears here as a reason for rank: filters decide
inclusion, and only the keys below decide order.

RankingKey.title: RankingKey
RankingKey.description: One ordering key, in the exact position the ``ORDER BY`` applies it.

RankingRoleContext.title: RankingRoleContext
RankingRoleContext.description:
Which stored rating supplies the RoleFit shown on every result.

``selected_role`` when the request carries ``role=<key>``: every result's
``result_role*`` group is that role. ``best_role`` otherwise: each player's own
stored best role, which may differ from row to row.

Whether that rating also *ordered* the page depends on the active sort, and
``detail`` says which of the two it is. Under the RoleFit modes the applicable
score and confidence are ordering keys; under Age, Expected Asking and Name they
are displayed context and the named sort does the ordering.
